scope: Himeji Castle inner citadel, Himeji (simplified schematic)
title: Himeji Castle
blurb: Japan’s White Heron Castle in Himeji, in simplified schematic form: the 46.4 m main keep and its cluster of smaller keeps, the maze of gates, stone walls and three moats — a fraction of the full 233-hectare complex.

systems.name: Keeps
systems.description: The 46.4 m main keep with its stone base, layered roofs and great pillars, plus the three subsidiary keeps of the cluster.

systems.name: Connecting corridors
systems.description: The roofed watariyagura passages linking the keeps, with the castle kitchen.

systems.name: Gates
systems.description: The Otemon main gate, the Hishi Gate, the Sakura bridge and the inner maze gates.

systems.name: Walls and turrets
systems.description: Battered stone walls, earthen walls, the oil wall, turret towers and wall defenses.

systems.name: West bailey
systems.description: Princess Sen’s Nishi-no-maru: the hundred-meter corridor and the Kesho Yagura.

systems.name: Moats and water
systems.description: The three concentric moats and the legendary Okiku well.

systems.name: Baileys and courtyards
systems.description: The walled baileys and courtyards between the gates.

explanations.main keep stone base: The great stone base carrying the main keep, with battered musha-gaeshi style walls; castle stone walls rise to 26 m at their highest. Exact base height is schematic.
explanations.main keep walls: The six wooden floors of the 46.4 m main keep, which shows five stories from outside: the second and third floors from the top read as one. The first floor is the 554 m2 thousand-mat room. Exact floor heights are schematic.
explanations.main keep roofs: The layered roof tiers of the keep, with karahafu and chidori hafu gables. White roof plaster seals the tiles against moisture and fire. Exact profiles are schematic.
explanations.main keep shachihoko: Golden shachihoko ornaments on the great roof ridge, believed to protect the castle from fire. Exact sculpture is schematic.
explanations.main keep great pillars: The two great pillars: the east pillar, 97 cm across at the base and originally a single fir tree, and the west pillar of Japanese cypress, replaced in the Showa restoration with a 26.4 m Kiso cypress. Exact positions are schematic.
explanations.main keep defenses: Steep misaligned staircases, bugukake weapon racks, corner strong points and stone-drop windows of the keep. Exact forms are schematic.
explanations.east small keep: The Higashi (east) small keep, one of three subsidiary keeps forming the cluster with the main keep. Exact height is schematic.
explanations.west small keep: The Nishi (west) small keep. Exact height is schematic.
explanations.northwest small keep: The Inui (northwest) small keep. Exact height is schematic.
explanations.connecting corridors: The roofed I, Ro, Ha and Ni watariyagura passages linking the keeps, National Treasures. Exact routes are schematic.
explanations.castle kitchen: The castle kitchen (daidokoro) beside the corridors. Exact placement is schematic.
explanations.sakura gate bridge: The Sakuramon-bashi wooden bridge to the Otemon, reconstructed in 2007 to the original Edo-period design. Exact span is schematic.
explanations.otemon main gate: The Otemon, great main gate of the castle. Exact form is schematic.
explanations.hishi gate: The Hishi (Diamond) Gate, main entrance to the castle proper, keeping its Azuchi-Momoyama appearance. Exact form is schematic.
explanations.inner maze gates: The I, Ro, Ha, Ni, Ho, He, Chi, Ri, Ru, Nu and Bizen gates along the winding approach. Exact placement is schematic.
explanations.mizuno gates: The three Mizuno gates on the western approach. Exact placement is schematic.
explanations.citadel stone walls: Battered stone walls of the inner citadel, toward the 26 m maximum of the castle’s stonework. Exact runs are schematic.
explanations.keep enclosure walls and platform: The raised platform and enclosure walls ringing the keep cluster. Exact extent is schematic.
explanations.outer earthen walls: Plastered earthen walls lining the outer baileys; 32 survive. Exact runs are schematic.
explanations.aburakabe oil wall: The Aburakabe oil wall, reported as clay, gravel and fermented rice water, extremely hard and fireproof. Single-source account; placement is schematic.
explanations.turret towers: Defensive turret towers on the citadel walls; 16 turrets are Important Cultural Properties. Exact placement is schematic.
explanations.ubagaishi millstone: The Ubagaishi: legend says an old woman donated her millstone for the walls, and it was set into the stonework. The tale is local legend.
explanations.wall loopholes and maze walls: Sama loopholes for matchlocks and bows, and low walls shaping the maze-like approach. Exact forms are schematic.
explanations.hyakken roka corridor: The Hyakken Roka, the hundred-meter roofed corridor of the west bailey, vital to the defense and once serving Princess Sen’s quarters. Exact length is schematic.
explanations.kesho yagura: The Kesho Yagura of the Nishi-no-maru, part of Princess Sen’s residence. Exact form is schematic.
explanations.nishi-no-maru grounds: The courtyard, wall and gate of the west bailey. Exact extent is schematic.
explanations.inner moat: The inner moat, the Sangoku-bori, ringing the citadel. Exact width and course are schematic.
explanations.middle and outer moats: The middle and outer moats; the area within the middle moat is a Special Historic Site. Exact courses are schematic.
explanations.okiku well: Okiku-ido, the old stone-lined well of the Banshu Sarayashiki ghost story. Exact form is schematic.
explanations.bizenmaru bailey: The Bizenmaru bailey courtyard east of the keep cluster. Exact extent is schematic.
explanations.ni-no-maru bailey: The second bailey courtyard, with the east gate that alone survives from Hideyoshi’s 1581 castle. Exact extent is schematic.
explanations.san-no-maru bailey: The third bailey courtyard. Exact extent is schematic.
explanations.harakiri-maru courtyard: The small Harakiri-maru courtyard, intended for ritual suicide but never used. Exact extent is schematic.
explanations.otemae entrance square: The entrance square before the Otemon. Exact extent is schematic.
